title: Getting Started with organoR
text: organoR creates organisational charts tidy management-relationship data. supports line dotted management, vacancies, cross-team managers, multiple managers profession-specific shading. main workflow : read data; validate structure; construct organisational graph; extract team subgraph; render one team teams; optionally shade one selected profession.
code: library(organoR)

title: Getting Started with organoR
text: package contains complex example dataset: data one row management relationship. required columns : name; grade; profession; team; manager; manager_type. employee line manager dotted manager appears multiple rows. Employee attributes must remain consistent across rows. vacancy represented setting name "Vacancy".
code: complex_path <- system.file(   "extdata",   "complex_org.csv",   package = "organoR" )  org <- read_org_data(complex_path)  org #> # A tibble: 14 × 6 #>    name              grade profession        team      manager      manager_type #>    <chr>             <chr> <chr>             <chr>     <chr>        <chr>        #>  1 Chief Analyst     C3    OR                Corporate NA           line         #>  2 Health Head       C2    OR                Health    Chief Analy… line         #>  3 Justice Head      C2    Economist         Justice   Chief Analy… line         #>  4 Education Head    C2    OR                Education Chief Analy… line         #>  5 Health Lead       C1    Statistician      Health    Health Head  line         #>  6 Health Analyst    B3    OR                Health    Health Lead  line         #>  7 Health Analyst    B3    OR                Health    Justice Head dotted       #>  8 Health Officer    B2    Social Researcher Health    Health Lead  line         #>  9 Justice Lead      C1    OR                Justice   Justice Head line         #> 10 Justice Analyst   B3    Economist         Justice   Justice Lead line         #> 11 Education Lead    C1    OR                Education Education H… line         #> 12 Education Analyst B3    OR                Education Education L… line         #> 13 Vacancy           B2    OR                Health    Health Lead  line         #> 14 Vacancy           B3    Statistician      Justice   Justice Lead line

title: Getting Started with organoR
text: default leave occupied positions white: Although occupied positions unshaded, borders retain colour associated grade. Vacancies continue use dedicated vacancy style.
code: render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   shaded_profession = NULL )

title: Getting Started with organoR
text: Set shaded_profession single profession name fill profession’s nodes corresponding grade colour. example, shade operational research positions: professions remain white. legend identifies: grade colours; shaded profession; professions; vacancies.
code: render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   shaded_profession = "OR" )

title: Getting Started with organoR
text: package treat operational research intrinsically different professions. example, shade statistician positions : graph can therefore rendered different professional audiences without changing underlying data.
code: render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   shaded_profession = "Statistician" )

title: Getting Started with organoR
text: rendered graphs use following encodings: grade controls border colour; selected profession receives solid grade-coloured fill; occupied positions receive white fill; vacancies receive vacancy fill dashed border; line management uses solid edges; dotted management uses dotted edges. Separating encodings allows grade, profession, vacancy status management type interpreted independently.

title: Getting Started with organoR
text: Create custom theme supplying named grade palette: Use rendering: selected profession filled custom grade colour.
code: custom_theme <- theme_scotgov(   colours = c(     C3 = "#003B5C",     C2 = "#0065BD",     C1 = "#4A90C2",     B3 = "#8FB7D4",     B2 = "#C2D8E8",     B1 = "#E8F1F7"   ) ) render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   theme = custom_theme,   shaded_profession = "OR" )

text: typical analysis script :
code: library(organoR)  org <- read_org_data(   "complex_org.csv" )  validate_org_data(org)  graph_parts <- build_graph(org)  health_graph <- get_team_subgraph(   data = org,   team = "Health" )  render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   shaded_profession = "OR" )  render_all_teams(   data = org,   output_file = "all-organograms.html",   shaded_profession = "OR" )

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: organoR creates organisational charts tidy management-relationship data. package supports: line dotted management relationships; employees one manager; team-specific organograms; managers belonging teams; recursively linked management hierarchies; vacancies; grade-based node colours; optional solid shading selected profession; consistent node sizing across organograms; top--bottom organisational layouts; legends describing grade colours node styles; rendering teams single HTML page.

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: Install package source directory : package development, use:
code: install.packages(   "path/to/organoR",   repos = NULL,   type = "source" ) devtools::load_all()

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: input tidy format, one row management relationship. following columns required: name: employee name, "Vacancy" unoccupied position; grade: organisational grade; profession: analytical profession; team: employee’s team; manager: name manager, NA root position; manager_type: either "line" "dotted". example: employee one manager appear multiple rows name, grade, profession team. employee must belong exactly one team.
code: org <- tibble::tribble(   ~name,             ~grade, ~profession,          ~team,      ~manager,        ~manager_type,   "Chief Analyst",   "C3",   "OR",                 "Corporate", NA,              "line",   "Health Head",     "C2",   "OR",                 "Health",    "Chief Analyst", "line",   "Health Lead",     "C1",   "Statistician",       "Health",    "Health Head",   "line",   "Health Analyst",  "B3",   "OR",                 "Health",    "Health Lead",   "line",   "Health Analyst",  "B3",   "OR",                 "Health",    "Chief Analyst", "dotted",   "Health Officer",  "B2",   "Social Researcher",  "Health",    "Health Lead",   "line",   "Vacancy",          "B3",   "Economist",          "Health",    "Health Lead",   "line" )

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: Read CSV file : Validate graph construction rendering: Validation checks include: required columns; supported grade values; recognised management types; consistent employee metadata; references managers exist data; circular management relationships; managers whose grade lower employee. Additional professions can used. may produce warning included package’s initially recognised set, prevent rendering.
code: library(organoR)  org <- read_org_data(   "complex_org.csv" ) validate_org_data(org)

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: Use build_graph() construct complete organisational network: result contains: nodes: employee vacancy attributes; edges: management relationships; graph: directed igraph object. package generates: deterministic employee_id employee; unique vacancy_id every vacancy row. Unique vacancy identifiers allow one vacancy grade, profession, team manager.
code: graph_parts <- build_graph(org)  graph_parts$nodes graph_parts$edges graph_parts$graph

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: Use get_team_subgraph() obtain one team’s subgraph: subgraph contains: employees belonging selected team; vacancies belonging selected team; managers belonging teams; recursively linked managers required connect hierarchy. include unrelated employees teams.
code: health_graph <- get_team_subgraph(   data = org,   team = "Health" )  health_graph$nodes health_graph$edges

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: Render single team : default, occupied nodes white fill.
code: render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health" )

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: Set shaded_profession apply solid grade-coloured shading one profession: shade statisticians instead: leave occupied positions unshaded: shading parameter affects node fill . change node labels, border colours, management relationships graph layout. Vacancies retain dedicated fill dashed outline regardless selected profession.
code: render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   shaded_profession = "OR" ) render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   shaded_profession = "Statistician" ) render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   shaded_profession = NULL )

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: Render every team HTML page : output contains: one organogram team; single legend top page; consistent node dimensions across graphs; centred graphs retain natural GraphViz dimensions. function also creates dependency directory: Keep HTML file dependency directory together moving sharing output. render professions without solid shading:
code: render_all_teams(   data = org,   output_file = "all-organograms.html",   shaded_profession = "OR" ) all-organograms.html all-organograms_files/ render_all_teams(   data = org,   output_file = "all-organograms.html",   shaded_profession = NULL )

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: organograms use separate visual properties different information: border colour represents grade; solid grade-coloured fill identifies selected shaded profession; white fill identifies occupied positions; vacancy fill dashed border identify vacancies; solid edges identify line management; dotted edges identify dotted management. selected profession therefore rendering choice rather package-level definition profession primary.

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: default theme created : Pass explicitly rendering: custom grade palette can supplied named vector: colour vector must include every supported grade.
code: theme <- theme_scotgov() render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   theme = theme,   shaded_profession = "OR" ) custom_theme <- theme_scotgov(   colours = c(     C3 = "#003B5C",     C2 = "#0065BD",     C1 = "#4A90C2",     B3 = "#8FB7D4",     B2 = "#C2D8E8",     B1 = "#E8F1F7"   ) )  render_team_org(   data = org,   team = "Health",   theme = custom_theme,   shaded_profession = "Statistician" )

title: Organisational Organograms from Tidy Data
text: package includes several example datasets: Load render complex example :
code: simple_path <- system.file(   "extdata",   "simple_org.csv",   package = "organoR" )  matrix_path <- system.file(   "extdata",   "matrix_org.csv",   package = "organoR" )  vacancy_path <- system.file(   "extdata",   "vacancy_org.csv",   package = "organoR" )  complex_path <- system.file(   "extdata",   "complex_org.csv",   package = "organoR" ) complex_org <- read_org_data(complex_path)  render_all_teams(   data = complex_org,   output_file = "complex-organograms.html",   shaded_profession = "OR" )
